Subject: Deployment mode evaluation & cost model - Acme

Hi Gabriel - great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery:

Summary of needs (what I captured):
- Primary use: real-time assistant + summarization for customer support workflows
- Expected monthly usage: ~1.5B input+output tokens (you said order of magnitude)
- Avg tokens per request: ~500 tokens
- Peak concurrent requests: ~20 workers/streams
- Data residency: EU (must keep data in EU region)
- Security: SOC2 + contractual controls; possibility of private VPC/on-prem for regulated flows

Deployment options we discussed (tradeoffs):
1) Hosted API - fastest to go live, pay per-token. Good for bursty/variable workloads; minimal ops.
2) Dedicated capacity - reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput. Lower unit cost for steady, high-volume workloads; supports commit pricing and autoscaling policies.
3) Private VPC / on-prem - full network isolation and control for regulated data; longer lead time and enterprise contract.

Ask / data we need from you to model pricing:
- Confirm monthly tokens (approximate is fine)
- % of traffic that must be EU-resident / private (if you need private for only sensitive flows vs all traffic)
- Expected SLOs (p99 latency targets) and acceptable fallbacks

I'll attach a simple cost worksheet with a back-of-envelope for Hosted vs Dedicated based on the numbers above. Next steps I suggest: you confirm the numbers, we produce a formal pricing worksheet + SOW draft, and schedule a pricing review with Procurement and Security on Wed (8/18).

Attaching: Redwood_Capacity_vs_Hosted_Costs_20260815.xlsx

Thanks - I will loop Marissa in on capacity economics and Neha on contractual/security items.

Hi Gabriel - looping in a quick cost-model primer to translate the choices into ballpark economics. Below are illustrative numbers (back-of-envelope) using your 1.5B token estimate. These are examples - we'll produce a formal workbook once you confirm the final token split and residency needs.

1) Hosted API (per-token):
- Example unit: $0.00060 per token (model variant + throughput tier)
- Monthly cost = 1,500,000,000 tokens * $0.00060 = $900,000 / month
- Pros: no infra commits, simple; Cons: higher unit cost for steady large volume, limited control over placement unless we use region-specific hosted endpoints.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) - commit example:
- Example commitment: reserved pool equivalent to sustained throughput for your peak ~20 concurrent streams.
- Reserved price: $40,000 / month (example for a modest dedicated pool) + variable overage.
- Effective unit cost (rough): if you amortize reserved cost across 1.5B tokens, ~ $0.000026 / token (=$40k / 1.5B) - in practice we size reserved pools to meet p99 latency and throughput so unit cost varies vs utilization.
- Pros: much lower unit cost for steady scale, deterministic latency; Cons: higher up-front commitment, longer provisioning lead time for Private/VPC variants.

3) Private VPC / On-prem:
- Higher setup and license/ops fees (one-time integration, networking, possible on-prem appliance). For regulated datasets this is often required; costs are driven by SOW (installation, network testing, support SLAs).

Recommended approach for Acme (based on tradeoffs):
- Short term (Q3): Start with EU-hosted endpoints for non-PII and a small-dedicated pool sized for POC of regulated flows to validate performance (2-4 week test).
- Medium term (Q4): Move regulated traffic to Dedicated (reserved) capacity in EU or Private VPC depending on legal/security sign-off. Dedicated gives much lower unit cost once steady-state is reached.

Next steps I can take:
- Produce a formal pricing workbook with a few committed-tier options and an SOW draft for EU Dedicated and Private VPC.
- Prep a comparison slide for Procurement showing total cost of ownership (12-month view).

Attached: SOW_draft_acme_v1.docx (starter). Will update numbers once you confirm token split and % of traffic that must be EU-resident.
